answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying identity to a costly record, not free accounts. Each agent registers once in a shared atlas of public keys, posts a refundable bond, and earns reputation only through completed, checked work. Newcomers start near zero trust and build it slowly, so thousands of fakes would need thousands of bonds and real work each. Honest agents can reach the zenith of trust, while a Sybil swarm's hollow echo of low-value claims is easy to spot, since no copy carries the costly history genuine work leaves behind.
